subject: Brightlane MAP: evaluation timeline + token/unit-econ assumptions
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightlane.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: 2028-08-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Brightlane MAP kickoff: eval plan + cost assumptions

Hi Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. Procurement asked me to get a mutual action plan in writing so they can align on internal approvals and the POC budget. Two specific asks from Brightlane: 1) a short evaluation timeline with milestones we can include in our SOW; and 2) a clear summary of the unit economics assumptions you used for the pilot (tokens/$, caching/prefetch expectations, batching guidance for our 95th percentile latency target).

Can your team draft a one-page MAP with those items and any gating criteria (QA pass, throughput verification) so I can circulate? We budgeted for a 6‑week POC but are willing to compress if the acceptance gates are clear.

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Gomez
Director of Data Products, Brightlane Analytics
alex.gomez@brightlane.ai

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightlane.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-21T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Brightlane MAP kickoff: eval plan + cost assumptions

Hi Alex — thanks, we can do that. Drafting notes below and will attach a formal MAP & spreadsheet in the next hour. High-level approach: 

- Target eval timeline: 4 weeks (1 week integration, 2 weeks traffic-based evaluation, 1 week acceptance + handoff). Can compress to 3 weeks if Brightlane provides a sample production traffic trace and agrees to a narrower acceptance window.
- Unit econ assumptions for pilot (conservative): tokens per query = 1.1k tokens average; tokens/$ (hosted, mixed model) = ~35,000 tokens per $1 for the recommended quantized variant; expected effective tokens/$ after KV prefix caching = ~60% uplift in tokens/$ for repeated contexts.
- Batching guidance: aim for 8–16 request batch sizes for heavy inference paths; prefer async batching for non-blocking prediction endpoints to keep p95 latency < 350ms.
- Prefetch/KV caching: recommend prefix caching for session-style flows (expected 15–30% token savings in first pass).
- Gating: successful 1k QPS throughput test at target p95 with <5% error rate, accuracy delta <2% vs baseline, and unit-econ validation within 15% of forecast.

I'll loop Karthik and Ben for any technical corrections — Ben will own cost-model worksheets. Expect attachments: "brightlane_map_v1.xlsx" (MAP + timeline + gating) and "token-econ-assumptions.pdf" (assumption rationale).

Best,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-21T13:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Brightlane MAP kickoff: eval plan + cost assumptions

Kim / Ben — quick technical clarifications on the assumptions so the MAP doesn't overpromise: 

- The 1.1k tokens/query avg looks fine for their demo data, but add a 20% high-tail buffer for edge cases (use 1.3k for cost worst-case in the spreadsheet).
- The 35k tokens/$ number depends on model + quantization level; call it a range 28k–38k tokens/$ and annotate which model variant that maps to (e.g., rw-medium-16q for the mid-range).
- KV caching uplift: 60% tokens/$ is optimistic; recommend using 40% uplift for acceptance gating and call out the optimistic vs conservative columns in the sheet.
- Batching: 8–16 is OK, but we need to call out latency tradeoffs at 16 for their p95 target — include a preflight microbenchmark (script attached) to validate p95 at candidate batch sizes.

Ben — can you update the workbook with conservative vs optimistic columns and a runbook entry for the microbenchmark? Priyom, please add the Ops mutual rollback/fallback policy and procurement triggers for dedicated capacity if they exceed X tokens/day.

--
Karthik
Principal Infra SRE, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightlane.ai>, procurement@brightlane.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-21T17:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Brightlane MAP kickoff: eval plan + cost assumptions

Alex — attaching the MAP and the unit-econ worksheet (see attachments). Summary below so procurement can include it in their packet: 

1) Condensed MAP & timeline (4-week plan):
   - Week 0: SOW sign + env provisioning (Redwood staging + Brightlane test tenant)
   - Week 1: Integration & smoke tests (sample dataset, baseline correctness checks)
   - Weeks 2–3: Traffic evaluation & performance tuning (batching, caching, quantization sweep)
   - Week 4: Acceptance (throughput/latency gates, cost verification) and handoff

2) Unit-econ highlights (conservative baseline used for procurement):
   - Cost baseline uses 1.3k tokens/query (20% high-tail buffer) and conservative tokens/$ = 30k (quantized medium model): projected pilot spend = $X (see workbook cell B12)
   - Conservative KV caching uplift: 40% (we show optimistic 60% in a separate column)
   - Batching guidance: start at batch size 8; validate 12 and 16 in microbench. If p95 rises >50ms at 16, fallback to 8–10.

3) Acceptance gates (must be met for pilot sign-off):
   - p95 latency <= 350ms on production-ish workload
   - throughput test: sustained 1k requests/minute with <5% errors
   - unit economics within 15% of conservative forecast

4) Contingency & procurement notes:
   - If daily token volume > 3M during pilot, ops recommends reserving Dedicated capacity; procurement triggers included in workbook.
   - We can compress to a 3-week MAP if Brightlane provides a production traffic trace and approves a narrower acceptance window.

Please confirm if this works for procurement and I'll convert the MAP to a signed SOW template.

Thanks — Kim

Attachments: brightlane_map_v1.xlsx (MAP + gating + timeline), token-econ-assumptions.pdf (detailed spreads and model mapping)
